#A Word of Caution

This is not a book of worship. It is not a book of summoning. It is a list of very powerful beings who do not have your interests at heart, compiled so that you may recognise their handiwork and walk the other way.

The scholars call them Daedric Princes. Common folk call them worse things, but quietly.

#What They Are

The Princes are not gods in the way the Divines are said to be. They did not help make the world and they do not feel bound to protect it. Each rules a realm of its own beyond the edges of ours, and each is concerned with some particular corner of mortal life: ambition, madness, the hunt, secrets, pleasure, decay.

They are not simply evil. Some of them have been known to reward courage, honesty or cleverness. But every reward comes with a hook, and the hook is always sharper than it looks.

#How to Recognise Their Interest

A shrine in a place where no shrine should be. A stranger who knows your name before you give it. A dream that repeats three nights running, always with the same voice. Animals that will not enter a certain valley.

If more than one of these things happens to you in the same season, I suggest a long trip somewhere far away and very dull.

#Their Servants

Lesser Daedra serve the Princes as soldiers and messengers. The ones most often seen in the north are the atronachs, living storms of flame, frost or lightning that mages bind for a short while to fight on their behalf.

A summoned atronach is not your friend. It is a prisoner doing its time. Treat it with the wary respect you would give a chained bear.

#The Golden Rule

Never accept a gift from a Prince without asking what it costs.

Never accept the answer as complete.
